verdict.rationale: Svelte is a compiler and framework that users install and run on their own machines. The evidence shows a public GitHub repository, local project creation via npm, local builds that output plain HTML/JS/CSS to a dist directory, and a static adapter, so nothing depends on a vendor-hosted service. However, the pack never explicitly states an open-source license or documents self-hosting as such, so coverage is only partial. Missing for 10: explicit open-source license evidence, explicit documentation framing local/self-hosted operation of the core product, independent corroboration of running it fully self-hosted.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: It's a compiler that takes your declarative components and converts them into efficient JavaScript that surgically updates the DOM.

npx sv create myapp
cd myapp
npm install
npm run dev
With this, `npm run build` will generate HTML, JS, and CSS files inside the `dist` directory.
You can use SvelteKit as a static site generator (SSG) that fully prerenders your site with static rendering using adapter-static.
claude mcp add -t stdio -s [scope] svelte -- npx -y @sveltejs/mcp
